summary: A form-associated toggle for an on/off setting that takes effect immediately. It submits a value when on, resets with its form, is disabled by a disabled fieldset, validates required, and has a label, a description, an error message and two sizes.

selected.note: On. Registered alias of the native checked. Changes by user action or by the author; a form reset restores the initial value (the markup attribute).

value.note: The string submitted under name while selected, like a native checkbox. Nothing is submitted while off.

name.note: The form field name. Without a name nothing is submitted.

disabled.note: Not focusable, not operable, not submitted. Also applied by an ancestor disabled fieldset, without overwriting this attribute (formDisabledCallback).

required.note: Must be on for the form to be valid; off is valueMissing. Matches a native required checkbox.

validation.note: error shows the error look and message and sets aria-invalid. Set by the author; the component also enters error after a failed validity check on form submit (invalid event).

label.note: Visible text and the accessible name. Without a label the author must give aria-label or aria-labelledby; otherwise a console warning is logged.

description.note: Hint under the label, linked with aria-describedby.

errorMessage.note: Why the value is not accepted. Shown, and described by aria-describedby, only while validation is error.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.notes: Host layout: control and text column side by side. Carries the host attributes disabled, required, validation, size.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: The focusable element with role=switch and aria-checked. Inside the shadow root; the form value lives on the host's ElementInternals.

anatomy.name: track
anatomy.notes: The pill-shaped groove. Fill changes with selected.

anatomy.name: thumb
anatomy.notes: The knob; moves along the track on toggle, without travel animation under prefers-reduced-motion.

anatomy.name: text
anatomy.notes: Column holding label, description and error message; absent when none are given.

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.notes: The label text. Clicking it toggles the switch.

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: The error message; rendered only in validation error and linked by aria-describedby.

label.notes: Visible label and accessible name; text only, also settable with the label property.

change.note: Fires after the user toggles it, once selected has changed. Not fired when the author sets selected.

input.note: Fires on each user toggle, before change. Read the new state from the element's selected property.

disabled.trigger: disabled, or disabled by a fieldset
disabled.note: Reduced opacity; no pointer events; not in the tab order.

accessibility.native: No native element has on/off semantics; input type=checkbox with role=switch is the closest. The component renders a focusable control with role=switch and aria-checked, per the WAI-ARIA APG Switch pattern.
accessibility.accessibleNameSource: label property, or the host's aria-label / aria-labelledby; clicking the label toggles the switch.

formAssociation.note: Through the shared FormAssociated mixin (ElementInternals): submits name=value while selected and nothing while off; form reset restores the initial selected; state restored on navigation; an ancestor disabled fieldset disables it; required sets valueMissing while off, with the validity anchored on the control.

accessibility.targetSize: Interactive area at least 24x24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8); the label is part of the click target.
accessibility.focusRingVisible: Ring with offset, 3:1 against adjacent colors, on :focus-visible only; not clipped by the host.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: Console warning when none of label, aria-label or aria-labelledby is present.

keyboard.Tab: Moves focus to the switch; disabled switches are skipped.
keyboard.Shift+Tab: Moves focus to the previous focusable element.
keyboard.Enter: Does nothing on the switch itself (optional in the APG); left free for implicit form submission (Q3).

aria: aria-describedby lists the description id and, while in error, the error id
announcements: Screen readers announce name, switch role and on/off state; the new state is announced after toggling without a live region.
On a failed submit focus moves to the first invalid switch, and its error message is read as its description.

useCases.when: A setting turns on or off and takes effect at once (notifications, dark mode).
An on/off choice is submitted with a form and applied on submit.
useCases.use: A checkbox; a switch implies immediate effect

antiPatterns.pattern: Several mutually exclusive options as switches
antiPatterns.why: A switch is a single boolean

openQuestions.question: Contract content drafted with the contract-author skill (visual reference, WAI-ARIA APG)?
openQuestions.recommendation: Draft from the visual reference docs and the APG Switch pattern.
openQuestions.answer: Drafted from the visual reference docs and the WAI-ARIA APG Switch pattern; the skill is staged, not installed, so its steps were followed by hand.

openQuestions.question: Name the on/off prop selected (registered, alias of checked) or checked?
openQuestions.recommendation: selected: registered in the API vocabulary, aliasing checked.

openQuestions.question: Which sizes?
openQuestions.recommendation: small and medium (vocabulary words; the size.switch tokens exist for both).

openQuestions.question: Does Enter toggle?
openQuestions.recommendation: No: Space only, as a native checkbox; Enter stays free for implicit form submit.

openQuestions.question: Are label, description and error message props or slots?
openQuestions.recommendation: Text props (registered label, description, errorMessage); keeps the accessible name simple.

openQuestions.question: What is submitted and when does validation show?
openQuestions.recommendation: name=value while on, nothing while off (native checkbox); error look on author-set validation or a failed submit, not on first render.

openQuestions.question: Is there an indeterminate or readOnly state?
openQuestions.recommendation: No: a switch is binary, and the APG gives readOnly no switch behavior.
